newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti has "useful" meeting with Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti has "useful" meeting with Prodi.

text.p: Fausto Bertinotti, leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party, said on Monday he had a useful meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi over the 1997 budget, but added they still had differences over the package.
"I think it was a useful meeting even if we are not in agreement on everything," Bertinotti told reporters after he met Prodi and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi.
"We repeated that we will not accept any tampering regarding protection of health and social security benefits and we will give our support only in that case," Bertinotti said.
The centre-left government aims to cut next year's public sector borrowing requirement by 32.4 trillion lire.
The package must be presented to parliament by September 30. Both chambers then have until December 31 to approve it.
Bertinotti's party holds the balance of power in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).
Bertinotti repeated, as he had said last week, that he believed the government's chances of winning approval in parliament for its budget package were 50-50.
"When one holds informal meetings such as these, the percentages do not vary because they can only change with official meetings," Bertinotti said. --Rome bureau, +00396 678 2501
